title: Predestination
scope: The 2014 film · the central character’s identity loop
premise: A bartender, a missing lover and an abandoned child appear to belong to different lives. How do they fit into the life first told as Jane’s story?
ending: Jane, John, the agent and the Fizzle Bomber are stages of one life. The child is also that same person: the story closes the parentage loop rather than providing an outside origin. Names here identify stages and roles; they do not imply separate people.

people.name: Jane / John / the agent
people.introduction: One person described by the names and roles used at different stages of their life.

events.title: A baby grows up as Jane
events.text: A baby is left at an orphanage and grows up as Jane. The identity of that child will connect the apparent beginning of this life to its later events.

events.title: Jane has a child with a stranger
events.text: Jane meets a man who later disappears. After childbirth and medical intervention, the character comes to live as John. The child is taken away.

events.title: John tells the bartender about that life
events.text: Now living as John, the person who grew up as Jane tells a bartender about the missing lover and child. The bartender is an agent who travels through time. He offers to take John back to confront the man who abandoned Jane.

events.title: John becomes the stranger Jane met
events.text: The journey into the past puts John in the role of Jane’s lover. The parents of the child are different stages of this same person.

events.title: The agent closes the child’s loop
events.text: John later becomes the agent—the same person as the bartender who offered him the journey. As the agent, he takes Jane’s baby back to the orphanage. That baby grows up as Jane, completing the circle.

events.title: The final enemy is another future stage
events.text: The agent confronts the Fizzle Bomber, the criminal he has been pursuing, and recognises an older version of himself. This brings another apparently separate person into the same life.
events.whenLabel: The confrontation with the older self

guide.title: Follow one life through its changing roles

chapters.title: Connect the apparent strangers
chapters.introduction: Connect the roles one at a time: John is the lover; the older John is the agent; the baby the agent carries is the child who grows up as Jane.

sources.title: Ethan Hawke and the Spierig brothers discuss the identity puzzle
sources.note: Interview conducted at SXSW 2014 and published 5 January 2015. Hawke discusses the audience recognising one person. It corroborates the broad identity premise, not every role, journey or claim about the ending.
